Derrick Burfitt was second in this race last year, but this time could not get nearer than eighth with Vern Blowfield ninth. As the first seven home included such runners as Alec Olney, D.

Held at Wimbledon on February 18th, and this was styled a " B " team fixture but as included in the Thames Valley team were such runners as Les Field and Alec Olney, the field was really much stronger than usual.

As regards Alec Olney's record breaking run on the first leg, this was simply superlative running, and when you think back on some of the well-known runners who have done this stage and yet not come within a minute of Olney's time, well all we can say is that Vern Blowfield was not disgraced in hand…
Held on Easter Monday, there was a very strong wind blowing, but conditions seemed to favour the runners and Alec Olney set up a new course record with a time of 50 mins. 52 secs.

Newell, who won our novices one mile back in the summer, finished well up and looks like being a decided asset to our ranks. Alec Olney, of T.V.H., took things steady and was content to finish in 14th place, as did A.

Walker off on the first stage to Purley and, although, as we anticipated, Alec Olney gave his club the lead, Chas. put up a fine run by handing over in 2nd place, just beating the Midland champion, C.

In the 100 yards " Ginger " Holtum finished second, with Bob Taylor in a similar position in the 880 yards. Ray Tooby was second in the 1 mile and Les Stokell was runner-up to Alec Olney in the 2 miles run.

Walker and Bill Lucas both run well, with the former beating Alec Olney for first place, with Bill third. It was only through Bill " pepping " up the pace with a lap to go that the field broke up and this enabled Walker to use his stronger finishing powers to good advantage.
Charlie Walker won the individual race beating Alec Olney and Ted Manley with Bill Lucas in 4th place, Ray Tooby 7th and Archie Bedford 8th.
Alec Olney was first home followed by Charlie Walker, and then came Ray Tooby, Eddie Short and Archie Bedford who ran in together, just in front of A.
Bill Lucas then took us to the front on the third stage but Vern Blowfield could not hold Alec Olney over the final "leg," and so we finished 2nd to Thames Valley H.

Ian Badiali could only finish 4th in the 440 final which was won in 50.7 secs, and it is a pity that we are forced to run Ian at this distance as we think he prefers the half-mile. Bill Lucas set up yet another "meet" record with his time of 14 min. 30.6 secs. in the 3 miles run, and he beat Alec Olney and K.
On the first stage from Mitcham to Purley we had Jack Brown, and he put up a truly magnificent performance to beat Alec Olney’s record time of 27.37 by five seconds.
Although there was a strong wind blowing the weather was fine, and Alec Olney beat his old record by 3 seconds, with a time of 49 mins. 40 secs.

However even Driver's time was not unbeatable, for first Jim Peters lowered it by 10 seconds and in doing so passed Charlie Walker and took Essex Beagles into 2nd place, and later by Alec Olney who reduced it by another 7 seconds without bringing his club T.V.H. anywhere near the front.

Our new Cross Country Captain, Eddie Short, then took over at Purley for the long grind to Earlswood and I suppose no one could wish for a less envious task than to chase Alec Olney of T.V.H. who must be considered one of the best road runners of all time.

They were followed in by the T.V.H. star Alec Olney and another young rising luminary Walter Hesketh from Manchester A.C. Lancashire were clear in the team championship with a fifty points margin over Warwickshire.
Willie Slykhuis must be favourite surely and Alec Olney was already making a name for himself. I decided to back Bill for 3rd (one of my class-mates had decided to run a book this year).
Gordon Pirie, Frank Sando, Alec Olney, John Parlett, Chris Chataway … these are just some of the stars of the ’50s & ’60s with whom Charlie tangled with over track, road and cross country.
